content.title: Material Text Effect | Clouds Form Words, Then Clear
content.summary: The same physical material first forms short, stable, and readable characters, then disperses back to its natural state in reverse along the original process.

quick_start.input_format: Single physical material + short word aggregation + readable pause + same physical reversal + complete reset without words
quick_start.recommended_input: Iron filings on the experimental plate above gather along magnetic field lines to form the word 'NORTH'. After becoming stable and readable, they disperse in reverse using the same particle physics, finally returning to the concentric magnetic field around the compass.
required_anchors: Use a single continuous physical material field before, during, and after the word.
Form one short, highly legible word through visible material aggregation.
Reverse using the same material physics that formed the word.
Return to a coherent non-text field with the original anchor still readable.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: The same physical material first forms short characters that are stable and readable, and then disperses back to its natural state in the reverse direction along the original process.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Let one continuous physical field reorganize into a short readable word, hold long enough for recognition, then reverse the same material process so the field returns to a coherent non-text state. Camera motion may reveal scale, but typography must remain an emergent material state rather than a pasted title.

invariants.rule: Use one continuous physical material field before, during and after the word.
invariants.ablation_failure: A separate title overlay breaks the effect.

invariants.rule: Form one short high-legibility word through visible material aggregation.
invariants.purpose: Makes recognition achievable within fifteen seconds.
invariants.ablation_failure: Long phrases or instant appearance weaken physical formation.

invariants.rule: Hold the complete word before reversal begins.
invariants.purpose: Gives viewers a clear proof state.
invariants.ablation_failure: Immediate dissolution makes the word feel accidental.

invariants.rule: Reverse using the same material physics that formed the word.
invariants.ablation_failure: A generic fade does not prove reversibility.

invariants.rule: Return to a coherent non-text field with the original anchor still readable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Residual letter fragments leave the loop incomplete.

slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
